title: Dissecting the genetic basis of yield stability in faba bean by multi-environment analysis.
data_url: Zenodo record https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.13908861 ('Genotypic and phenotypic data for the ProFaba diverse panel of faba bean accessions', type 'Dataset', published 2024-10-09, licence cc-by-4.0). Four files, 36,398,614 bytes total, all of which I downloaded: Readme.txt 6,501 bytes; final_profaba_db.txt 2,814,442 bytes (the curated plot-level phenotype table); ProFaba_db_complete.7z 742,115 bytes (eight CSV files, the full relational field database); ProFaba_chrAll_QUAL20_MQ20_2snp_miss20_het0.1_maf0.05_SNPnames.vcf.gz 32,835,556 bytes (the marker matrix). Supplementary tables: https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC13383516/supplementaryFiles (10,511,720-byte zip; MOESM2 xlsx 717,761 bytes holds Tables S1-S11). Raw reads, which I did NOT download by policy: European Nucleotide Archive projects PRJEB94134 (whole-genome resequencing) and PRJEB85172 (targeted capture, 239 runs).

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Europe PMC search on the DOI returned exactly 1 hit (PMID 42477785, PMCID PMC13383516, isOpenAccess 'Y', licence 'cc by', first published 2026-07-20) and the full-text XML downloaded cleanly (263,649 characters). I downloaded all four Zenodo files (36,398,614 bytes total) and the Europe PMC supplementary zip, extracted the 7z archive with bsdtar (no 7z binary on this machine) and parsed every file myself. PHENOTYPES, final_profaba_db.txt: 38,071 data rows plus a header, 7 tab-separated quoted columns (Trait, TRID, Block, Row, GPID, Score, env_mean). I counted 14 traits, 12 environments, 223 accession identifiers, 2 blocks, 58 row positions. ZERO missing Score values and ZERO non-numeric Score values. The deposited env_mean column reproduces exactly from the Score column (for example Flowering time at RAGT003: stated 63.3609865470852, my recomputation 63.360987), and no trait-environment pair carries two different env_mean values. Per-trait counts I measured: Plant height at end of flowering 4,674 plots / 12 environments; Flowering time 4,364 / 11; Seed yield 3,747 / 9; Branch number per plant 3,290 / 9; End of flowering 3,172 / 8; Plant height at maturity 2,766 / 7; Flower number per node 2,350 / 6; Rust 2,315 / 6; Seed number per pod 2,292 / 6; Pod number per node 2,041 / 6; First pod position 2,039 / 6; Pod length 2,001 / 6; Field emergence 1,715 / 4; Vigor 1,305 / 3. Distinct trait-by-genotype-by-environment cells: 20,493. Seed yield alone: 1,849 genotype-by-environment cells. MARKERS, the VCF: I streamed the whole gzip file in 2.2 seconds and counted exactly 539,643 variants and exactly 222 samples, 24 header meta lines, source 'beagle.22Jul22.46e.jar', FORMAT is GT only, all genotypes phased, ZERO missing genotype fields in the first 2,000 variants, minor allele frequency minimum 0.0518 / median 0.1239 / maximum 0.5, variants per chromosome 1:77,450 2:82,215 3:88,487 4:81,966 5:76,113 6:67,810 7:65,602. Uncompressed text is 511,180,212 bytes; as an int8 dosage matrix it is 539,643 x 222 = 119,800,746 bytes. THE JOIN: all 222 VCF samples are present in the phenotype file; exactly one phenotyped accession, GPID_00246, is absent from the VCF, and I identified it from ProGP.csv as 'Tiffany' with the comment 'check-Tiffany' - the repeated check variety. It carries 2,463 of the 38,071 plot rows (307 of them seed yield), so dropping it leaves 35,608 rows on 222 lines that join 222 of 222 to the markers. DUPLICATES: 561 duplicate (Trait, TRID, Block, Row, GPID) keys contributing 1,062 extra rows; 535 of those 561 keys belong to GPID_00246, leaving only 26 duplicate keys on three real accessions (GPID_00097, GPID_00011, GPID_00152), median relative range 0.082. UNITS: supplementary Table S6, which I parsed with my own xlsx reader, gives a Unit and a Transformation for all 14 traits (Seed yield g/m2, Flowering time and End of flowering days, four heights/lengths cm, four counts, three 1-9 or 0-10 scores; transformations: Cubic for Field emergence, Square root for Rust, Square for Vigor, None for the other eleven). NOISE FLOOR, measured from the two replicate blocks: median within-cell coefficient of variation 0.218 for seed yield, 0.064 for plant height at maturity, 0.011 for flowering time; per-environment approximate repeatability for seed yield 0.63 to 0.93. DUMMY BASELINES I computed at plot level for seed yield (n=3,747, mean 245.2 g/m2, standard deviation 184.5): per-environment mean explains R-squared 0.264, per-genotype mean 0.276. G-BY-E SIGNAL: across the 36 environment pairs with at least 30 shared lines, the correlation of line means for seed yield has median +0.474, minimum -0.192 (AGVG002 against GOET004, 215 shared lines) and maximum +0.800 (AGVG001 against AGVG002, 204 shared lines) - real re-ranking. THE CHEAPEST KILLING CHECK, ALREADY RUN: across the 9 environments that have seed yield, the paper's own weather-derived synthetic covariate synCov (read from Table S5) correlates with environment-mean seed yield at r = -0.218. Per trait the same correlation is +0.445, -0.117, -0.991 (on 4 points), +0.525, +0.533, +0.257, +0.389, +0.513, +0.703, -0.421, +0.760, +0.659, -0.218 and -0.833 (on 3 points). SUPPLEMENTS I parsed myself: Table S1 101 association rows x 52 columns; Table S2 190 rows x 34 columns with effect sizes and p-values from three methods; Table S3 123 set-based rows; Table S4 a 222-line x 107-SNP dosage matrix (0/1/2) whose line set equals the VCF sample set exactly; Table S5 12 environments with latitude, longitude, start and end dates, country, synCov and partner; Table S6 the units table; Table S7 223 rows (222 named lines plus one blank) with country of origin (31 distinct, 56 unknown), Spring_type 188 / Winter_type 30 / unknown 5, ADMIXTURE group sp1 89 / sp2 85 / sp4 34 / sp3 14, a distinct ENA BioSample accession per line, and adjusted line means for all 14 traits with at most 6 of 223 missing per trait; Table S8 the 9 NASA POWER weather variables; Table S9 9,264 SNP variant consequences; Table S10 the 33 lines shared with the NORFAB panel plus their genomic correlations (0.965 to 0.984 for the top five); Table S11 424 rows of per-line sequencing statistics. I also extracted Extended Data Table S1 from the Additional file 3 Word document: SNP heritability (PVE) for the seed yield intercept is 0.89 (SD 0.04), and PVE reaches 0.97-0.99 for branch number, end of flowering, flower number per node and pod length. WEATHER IN THE DEPOSIT, ProCL.csv: 2,712 daily rows over 37 trial identifiers, of which 26 have a single row; missingness is 65.0% for SunHours and DroughtIndex, 40.8% for reference evapotranspiration, 32.8% for day length, 18.3% for maximum and minimum temperature, 6.6% for mean temperature and precipitation. REFERENCE GENOME: the NCBI datasets API reports the Hedin/2 v2 assembly GCA_964205075.1 at 12,046,016,411 bases. BACKBONE LICENCES, checked on the HuggingFace API: InstaDeepAI/agro-nucleotide-transformer-1b is cc-by-nc-sa-4.0, kuleshov-group/PlantCaduceus_l20 and _l24 are apache-2.0, Prior-Labs/TabPFN-v2-reg is licence 'other'. ENA: PRJEB94134 returns whole-genome-sequencing runs of 86 to 173 gigabases each and PRJEB85172 returns 239 targeted-capture runs; I only read the file report and downloaded no reads.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Everything about how the panel and the markers were built, because no deposited file records it: the original 234-line panel, genotyping by single primer enrichment technology (90K probes) plus genotyping-by-sequencing, the 90-million-variant raw call set, the filtering cascade, the 347 K markers validated against 10-fold whole-genome resequencing, the 98.3% concordance on the shared Hedin/2 genotype, the 220 K linkage-disequilibrium-clumped subset, the 44.08 kb half-decay distance, nucleotide diversity 0.25, mean heterozygosity 4.48%. The published prediction numbers are text-only: 5-fold cross-validation repeated 100 times with the R package rrBLUP gave predictive ability 0.75 for mean seed yield, 0.76 for the slope on an unknown covariate and 0.55 for the slope on the synthetic covariate, with intercept predictive abilities ranging 0.50 (pod number per node) to 0.86 (flower number per node). The leave-one-environment-out comparison against the Jarquin et al. 2014 multiplicative reaction-norm model exists only as Additional file 3 Figure S2, a figure, so I could not read any number off it. The whole synthetic-covariate construction is paper-text-only AND NOT REPRODUCIBLE FROM THE DEPOSIT: the paper says 200 coordinates were sampled per country and reduced to 299 distinct points whose 9 NASA POWER season averages were put through principal component analysis, but those 299 coordinates are in no file, so the only thing I have is the 12 final synCov scores in Table S5. Two further gaps I confirmed by looking rather than assuming: the VCF INFO field retains only MAF, with no IMP flag on any of the 539,643 variants and no Beagle dosage-R-squared, so which individual calls were imputed and how well is UNAUDITABLE from the deposit; and the intercept and slope latent variables that the paper's genome-wide association and prediction analyses actually target are not deposited in any file. One unit disagreement I could not fully settle: supplementary Table S6 states Seed yield in g/m2, while the raw database dictionary ProPD.csv defines trait 20 'Seed yield' as 'the weight of seeds after pod threshing - in g' and a separate trait 52 as 'Yield per square meter (in g) calculated from PDID 20'; the magnitudes in the curated file (environment medians 93 to 392) are consistent with g/m2, so Table S6 is probably right, but the two documents contradict each other. I also did not verify whether Vicia faba is inside the pretraining corpus of AgroNT or PlantCaduceus, I ran none of the published models, and I reproduced none of the published prediction numbers. I did not open ProPH.csv's 110,701 rows beyond the header, and I did not read the Additional file 1 figures.

a1_downloadable.note: Passes, checked in the files. No login and no access application: all four Zenodo files (36,398,614 bytes) downloaded on the first try under CC BY 4.0, and the supplementary tables came through the Europe PMC supplementary-files endpoint. The only things behind a wall are the raw read archives (PRJEB94134, PRJEB85172), which the project does not need and which policy forbids downloading.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Passes for the plot-level framing, which is the one I propose. The label is literally the 'Score' column of final_profaba_db.txt: 38,071 field measurements, each already tagged with its trait, environment, block, row and accession. Nothing has to be constructed. It would FAIL for the framing the paper itself uses: the intercept and slope latent variables its association and prediction analyses target are not in any file and would have to be built by re-fitting a Bayesian reaction-norm model first.

a3_inputs_present.note: Passes, tested rather than assumed. The marker matrix is in the deposit as actual genotypes, not accessions: 539,643 variants by 222 samples, zero missing fields, and the sample names are the same GPID codes as the phenotype file, so all 222 join with no identifier resolution. Environment inputs are partly present (latitude, longitude, start and end date in Table S5, plus the 12 ready-made synCov scores) but the richer weather series must be re-pulled from the free NASA POWER interface, and the deposit's own weather file ProCL.csv is 65% empty for sun hours and drought index.

a4_units_stated.note: Passes, and better than most. Supplementary Table S6 gives a Unit and a Transformation for every one of the 14 traits (g/m2, days, cm, counts, 1-9 and 0-10 scores; Cubic, Square root and Square transformations named for three traits). One documented contradiction to carry forward: the raw database dictionary calls Seed yield 'weight of seeds after pod threshing - in g' and defines yield per square metre as a separate trait, so the two documents disagree on which one the curated file holds; the magnitudes (environment medians 93-392) favour Table S6's g/m2.

a5_enough_rows.note: Passes on the letter, and I am flagging loudly that it is borderline in substance. Verified counts: 38,071 labelled plot rows, 35,608 after dropping the ungenotyped check variety, 20,493 distinct trait-by-genotype-by-environment cells, 1,849 cells for seed yield. But the units a model must generalise over are only 222 inbred lines and 12 environments (9 for seed yield), against 539,643 markers. This is the same shape as the rejected scCT-DB candidate: the row count looks comfortable and the number of independent units does not. It is why Part C and Part I score low below.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: About 0.2 GB. The marker matrix becomes 539,643 x 222 int8 = 119,800,746 bytes; the phenotype table is 2,814,442 bytes; the supplementary workbook is 717,761 bytes. The genomic relationship matrix is only 222 x 222. The 511,180,212-byte uncompressed VCF text is transient and streams in 2.2 seconds, which I timed.
a6_fits_laptop.note: Passes easily for the tabular route, no graphics card needed. It would FAIL for any route that needs sequence context around the markers: the Hedin/2 v2 reference assembly is 12,046,016,411 bases, which I confirmed from the NCBI datasets interface, so feeding a plant DNA language model would mean a multi-gigabyte download and is off the table here.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Passes, with everything important matching. The VCF holds exactly 539,643 variants and exactly 222 samples, matching the deposit README and the paper's '540 K'; 14 traits, 12 environments and 2 blocks all match; Table S5 lists exactly 12 environments; Table S4's line set equals the VCF sample set exactly. The one apparent mismatch is explainable and I resolved it: the phenotype file has 223 accessions against the paper's 222 because the extra one is the replicated check variety Tiffany, which has no genotype. Two counts I could not check because the underlying data is not deposited: the 347 K markers said to be validated by resequencing, and the 299 random weather coordinates behind the synthetic covariate.

a8_label_provenance.note: Passes for the plot-level label. Every Score is a physical field measurement - seed weight after threshing, days from sowing to flowering, centimetres, counts, visual severity scores - made by named staff at seven sites, and none of it is any model's output. Three nearby framings would FAIL A8 and I am naming them so nobody drifts into them: (1) Table S7's 'adjusted line means' are shrunken mixed-model estimates, not raw means (for GPID_00001 seed yield Table S7 says 201.40 while the raw plot mean is 249.49), so training on them means distilling the authors' model; (2) the reaction-norm intercepts and slopes are outputs of a Bayesian model fitted to the very same plot data, so predicting them is distillation plus partial leakage; (3) the feature side is itself partly model output, because all missing genotypes were filled in by Beagle 5.4 and the deposited VCF retains no IMP flag and no dosage-R-squared on any of the 539,643 variants, so the imputed fraction cannot be audited.

B1.why: Three sources, one perfect key: 222/222 accession codes join phenotype table, VCF and Table S4. Counted, not assumed.

B2.why: Phenotype table, VCF and xlsx parsed first try; ProGP.csv is not valid UTF-8, and 7z needed bsdtar.

B3.why: Table S6 names unit and transformation per trait, but seven partners scored visually and ProPD contradicts S6 on yield units.

B4.why: Counted zero missing and zero non-numeric Score values in all 38,071 rows; no censored or qualitative entries anywhere.

B5.why: 561 duplicate keys / 1,062 extra rows, but 535 belong to the ungenotyped check variety; 26 remain, median relative range 0.082.

B6.why: README documents every file and column, Table S6 gives units plus transformations, ProPD gives the scoring method per trait.

C1.why: Accuracy-decay-with-weather-distance framing informs either way, but a decay curve from 9-12 environments is too noisy to trust.

C2.why: Several open, honestly split models exist: Genomes-to-Fields held-out-environment competition, GEFormer, GE-BiFormer, EnvRtype, a 14-dataset deep-learning-versus-GBLUP benchmark.

C3.why: Diversity angle is real - faba bean, not maize or wheat - but weakened because the authors already ran the standard model.

C4.why: Replacing field testing is genuinely expensive: 12 trials, 7 locations, 5 countries, 3 seasons, 7 partner organisations, verified in Table S5.

C5.why: Published numbers in text (0.75 yield mean, 0.76 and 0.55 for slopes, intercepts 0.50-0.86) plus dummy baselines I computed myself.

D1.why: Open weights exist (PlantCaduceus Apache-2.0, TabPFN-v2) but neither consumes a marker dosage matrix; checked both on HuggingFace.

D2.why: TabPFN-v2 needs no training at all and 222 rows fit its in-context window on a laptop processor; no embedding cache needed.

D3.why: Data is CC BY 4.0, PlantCaduceus Apache-2.0, but AgroNT is non-commercial and TabPFN's HuggingFace licence field reads only 'other'.

E1.why: Leave-one-environment-out (12 environments) and leave-one-country-out (5 countries) both buildable from Table S5; also a 2020/2021 year split.

E2.why: Counted 12 environments, 9 with seed yield, 5 countries, 7 locations and 4 ADMIXTURE subpopulations (89/85/34/14 lines) as holdout groups.

E3.why: I computed them: per-environment mean explains R-squared 0.264 and per-genotype mean 0.276 of plot-level seed yield variance.

E4.why: Two replicate blocks give a measured floor: median within-cell variation 21.8% for yield, 6.4% height, 1.1% flowering time.

E5.why: Verified controls available: 30 winter-type lines versus 188 spring, four ADMIXTURE groups, and the Tiffany check in every trial.

E6.why: Label shuffling, within-environment shuffling and marker-block ablation all cheap: the whole marker matrix streams in 2.2 seconds.

E7.why: Table S10 maps 33 lines to the independent NORFAB panel; plus a 2020-versus-2021 split and separate published faba bean panels.

E8.why: GBLUP on Table S7 means plus the deposited markers approximates the published 0.75; exact intercept values are not deposited.

G1.why: ENA BioSample accessions for all 222 lines and latitude/longitude per site, but gene and marker IDs are assembly-private.

G2.why: NASA POWER weather joins on latitude, longitude and date - the exact interface the authors used; SoilGrids joins the same key.

G3.why: One environment maps to one daily weather series, collapsed by season averaging; the 33-line NORFAB overlap is one-to-one.

G4.why: Combined question is writable: can a continent-wide weather grid predict line re-ranking at sites never trialled?

H1.why: A designed trial, so failures are recorded: yields span 0.694 to 1,255 g/m2 and poorly adapted exotic lines stayed in.

H2.why: 5 countries and 31 origin countries, but one species, one panel, Europe-only sites, only 2020-2021, only 2 blocks.

H3.why: Honest claim written out in one sentence below; the 222-line, 12-environment, Europe-only restriction is the whole of it.

H4.why: Paper flags missing trait-environment combinations (Fig S2), names limited sample size, and Table S6 documents every transformation.

I1.why: Named, and three are commercial: NPZ Innovation, Sejet Plant Breeding, Agrovegetal, RAGT, Agri Obtentions, IFAPA, Aarhus quantitative genetics.

I2.why: A trustworthy adaptation map would redirect trial siting, but the paper already handed them a fitted model.

I3.why: Breeders need a ranking to advance lines; the published metric is a correlation, roughly but not exactly that decision.

I4.why: At 222 lines and 540k markers a linear mixed model is the right tool; the per-genotype mean alone already explains 27.6%.

J1.why: Real grouped and leave-one-environment-out evaluation, but mostly kernel ridge regression and no sequence transfer learning.

J2.why: Yields in g/m2 and repeatabilities 0.63-0.93 are checkable, but mixed-model diagnostics need a quantitative geneticist I have not lined up.

J3.why: The joined, unit-documented 35,608-row table plus the synCov-versus-yield finding is shareable alone; I built most of it today.

J4.why: Roughly two to three weeks is statable, but no time budget is written down anywhere in the repository.

J5.why: No kill date and no condition recorded; nothing in NOTES.md.

existing_models.name: Genomes to Fields (G2F) Maize Genotype-by-Environment Prediction Competition (public multi-environment benchmark with held-out-environment scoring)
existing_models.score_and_split: I read the competition description, not a results table, so I quote no number. It releases maize trial data from 2014 to 2023 with genotypes, soil variables, weather records and 654 environmental covariates, and scores three breeding-relevant splits explicitly: known lines in unseen environments, new lines in known environments, and new lines in entirely untested environments - exactly the split this faba bean project would use.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: The organisers single out the hardest of their three scenarios, new genotypes in entirely untested environments, as the open problem.

existing_models.name: Jarquin et al. 2014 multiplicative reaction-norm model (genomic prediction with an environmental covariance matrix; the field's standard genotype-by-environment model)
existing_models.score_and_split: This paper itself ran it as the comparison under leave-one-environment-out and reports only that its own synthetic-covariate model gave 'predictive abilities in the same range'. The actual numbers live in Additional file 3 Figure S2, a figure, so I could not read them. Implemented in the open R package BGLR.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: The faba bean authors name the limitation of the unknown-covariate alternative: it cannot predict for untested environments at all, which is the gap their synthetic covariate is meant to fill.

existing_models.name: GEFormer and GE-BiFormer (transformer models that fuse marker and environmental data for genotype-by-environment prediction in maize)
existing_models.score_and_split: Found by search; I read titles and summaries only and retrieved no results table, so I quote no number. GE-BiFormer is reported to beat comparison methods under its harder validation scenarios using bidirectional cross-attention between genomic and environmental inputs. I did not confirm whether weights or code are public.

existing_models.name: Deep-learning-versus-GBLUP benchmark across 14 plant breeding datasets (Frontiers in Genetics 2025) and the earlier dense-architecture multi-environment deep learner (G3 2018)
existing_models.score_and_split: From the search summaries only: the 2018 multi-environment study found GBLUP best in 8 of 9 datasets once genotype-by-environment interaction was modelled, and the 2025 benchmark found neither deep learning nor GBLUP consistently ahead across 14 datasets, with deep learning doing relatively better on SMALL datasets. I did not retrieve either full text and quote no exact figure.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Both lines of work conclude that the choice of method depends on the trait and that deep learning gains require careful tuning - i.e. no method dominates, which is the honest state of the field.

existing_models.name: Faba-bean-specific prior work: a 90K single-primer-enrichment GWAS plus genomic selection study on 245 accessions with 38,014 markers (BMC Plant Biology 2025), genomic prediction for heat and herbicide tolerance in faba bean (2025), and an explainable TabPFN model for single-plant faba bean yield (Agronomy 2026)
existing_models.score_and_split: Found by search; I read only titles and summary text. The TabPFN paper reports R-squared 0.8746, root-mean-square error 1.9132 g per plant, mean absolute error 1.0819 and mean absolute percentage error 8.16% for plot-mean single-plant yield, but on its own trial data with a split I did not verify. The 245-accession study is an independent panel and so is a candidate external-validation set rather than only a competitor.

existing_models.name: Plant DNA language models with open weights: PlantCaduceus (16 angiosperm genomes, Apache-2.0) and AgroNT (48 plant species, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)
existing_models.score_and_split: I verified licences and downloadable checkpoints on the HuggingFace interface, nothing more. Neither was built for this task: both score variant effects and regulatory annotation from sequence, and I retrieved no genomic-prediction number for either. Reported cross-species strength for PlantCaduceus (average precision-recall area under curve 0.764) comes from the search summary, not a full text I read.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Not retrieved. The practical blocker I did verify is that using them here needs sequence windows from the 12,046,016,411-base Hedin/2 v2 assembly.

backbone.name: TabPFN-v2-reg (Prior-Labs/TabPFN-v2-reg, a pretrained transformer for small tabular regression that predicts by in-context learning with no training step), on principal components of the genomic relationship matrix plus season-aggregated weather variables. Secondary, and I am flagging it as blocked rather than recommending it: PlantCaduceus_l20 (a plant DNA language model, Apache-2.0) for sequence windows around markers.
backbone.hardware: Laptop processor only, 16 GB memory. The marker matrix streams in 2.2 seconds (timed) into a 119,800,746-byte int8 array; the genomic relationship matrix is 222 x 222 and its eigendecomposition is instant; TabPFN sees at most a few thousand rows and a few hundred columns, well inside its comfort zone. No embedding cache is required because this route never touches DNA sequence.
backbone.licence: The data is CC BY 4.0, which is clean. PlantCaduceus is Apache-2.0. AgroNT is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, so non-commercial only - a real problem given that three co-author organisations are commercial breeders. TabPFN-v2's HuggingFace licence field reads only 'other' (the Prior Labs licence), which I did not read in full, so treat it as unclear.

integration.partner_dataset: NASA POWER (the free satellite-and-reanalysis daily weather service the authors themselves used, via the R package nasapower) as the primary partner, with SoilGrids on the same key, the NORFAB faba bean diversity panel as an independent genotype partner, and the Genomes to Fields maize multi-environment resource as a cross-crop partner on environmental covariates.
integration.join_key: Latitude, longitude and the sowing-to-harvest date window, all four of which are in supplementary Table S5 for every one of the 12 environments (for example 37.45535, -6.36358, Excel serial dates 43801 to 44013 for the Spanish 2019/20 trial). That is one weather series per environment, collapsed to season averages - clean one-to-many. The independent-panel join uses Table S10, which maps 33 ProFaba accession codes to NORFAB line names one-to-one with genomic correlations of 0.965 to 0.984. All 222 lines also carry a distinct ENA BioSample accession, which is a standard identifier.
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Can a weather index computed over a dense grid of European locations predict which faba bean lines will change rank at a site that was never trialled, turning 12 field trials into a continent-wide adaptation map? Honest caveat: with only 12 environments the answer will have very wide error bars, and the single environmental index the authors supply correlates with environment-mean seed yield at only r = -0.218 across the 9 yield environments, which I measured.

controls.positive_control: Three, chosen before looking at a model result and all verified present in the files. (1) The 30 winter-type against the 188 spring-type lines must separate sharply on flowering time in the autumn-sown Spanish trials - a textbook effect; if the model misses it the plumbing is wrong. (2) The four ADMIXTURE subpopulations (89 / 85 / 34 / 14 lines) must recover the direction the paper reports: Mediterranean sp1 lines favoured as environments shift warm and dry, Central-and-Northern-European sp2 and Asian sp3 lines the opposite. (3) The check variety Tiffany, replicated 307 times across the yield trials, is the best-characterised entity in the dataset and should be among the easiest predictions - except that it has no genotype, which is itself worth knowing.
controls.negative_control: Shuffle the Score labels within trait and re-run: plot-level accuracy must collapse to the per-environment mean baseline I measured at R-squared 0.264. Then shuffle labels within environment only, to confirm the leave-one-environment-out grouping is actually grouping. Then replace the 539,643 markers with random columns of the same shape and confirm it matches the per-genotype-mean baseline of R-squared 0.276. Each full re-run costs minutes because the marker matrix streams in 2.2 seconds, which I timed.
controls.external_validation: Four options, in order of strength. (1) The independent NORFAB panel: Table S10 gives a verified one-to-one mapping for 33 shared lines. (2) A separate published faba bean panel of 245 accessions with 38,014 markers and its own trials - genuinely independent trials and curation, though I did not download it. (3) A year split inside this data: the 12 environments divide into six 2020-harvest and six 2021-harvest sites (five against four for seed yield), which costs one line of code and tests whether the model works on the season that came next. (4) A country split: Spain 2, Germany 3, Denmark 2, Ireland 1, France 4, giving five leave-one-country-out folds.

honest_claim_h3: Among 222 inbred faba bean lines that a European consortium chose to trial at seven sites in five countries during 2020 and 2021, markers plus a season-average weather index rank line performance this well at a site held out of training - and it says nothing about lines outside this panel, about sites outside north-western and Mediterranean Europe, or about seasons unlike those two.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use a plant variety's genetic markers plus the season's weather to predict how well it will yield at a field site never tested.
plain_idea.train_on: Each example is one field plot: the accession's 539,643 marker genotypes (verified present, zero missing) plus the sowing-to-harvest weather of that site and season. I counted 38,071 labelled plots, 35,608 once the ungenotyped check variety is dropped, covering 222 accessions, 12 site-by-year environments and 14 traits.
plain_idea.predict: The measured trait value for that plot - most importantly seed yield in grams per square metre. The true answer is a physical field measurement: seeds threshed from the plot and weighed, or days counted from sowing to flowering, or heights measured in centimetres, all made by named staff at seven partner sites.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Faba bean breeders at the named companies in this consortium (NPZ Innovation, Sejet Plant Breeding, Agrovegetal, RAGT, Agri Obtentions) each run expensive multi-site trials; a trustworthy prediction for an untrialled site would let them cut trial locations or choose better ones. Even a negative result is useful, because it would quantify how little a single weather index buys you when you have only a dozen environments.

ml_idea: Build the feature and label table nobody has shipped: 35,608 plot measurements on 222 genotyped faba bean lines across 12 European environments, joined to the 539,643-marker matrix on the accession code (222 of 222, verified) and to NASA POWER season-aggregate weather on latitude, longitude and the sowing-to-harvest window from Table S5. Then ask the one question that informs either way - how does prediction accuracy decay as the held-out environment gets further from the training environments in weather space? Evaluate under leave-one-environment-out (12 folds), leave-one-country-out (5 folds) and a 2020-versus-2021 year split, against three baselines I have already computed (global mean, per-environment mean R-squared 0.264, per-genotype mean R-squared 0.276) and against the published GBLUP predictive ability of 0.75 for mean seed yield. Compare a genomic-relationship ridge model, gradient boosting on genomic principal components crossed with weather variables, and TabPFN-v2 (a pretrained small-tabular transformer that needs no training). The honest expected outcome is parity with the mixed model the authors already fitted, because the effective sample size is 222 lines and 9 yield environments, and because the measured within-plot replicate variation for yield is already 21.8%. The only framing with a genuinely unloseable shape would be cross-crop transfer - does an environment-response model trained on the Genomes to Fields maize resource transfer to faba bean? - but genotypes do not transfer across species, so only the environment side could, and that is a thin thread to hang a project on.

effort.compute_note: Measured, not guessed, for the parts I ran: streaming all 539,643 variants by 222 samples of the VCF took 2.2 seconds on this laptop, and the resulting int8 dosage matrix is exactly 119,800,746 bytes; the 38,071-row phenotype table, all eight relational CSV files and all 11 supplementary tables parsed in under a second each. Peak memory of 2 GB and the 10-minute cross-validation figure are ESTIMATES: the genomic relationship matrix is only 222 x 222 so its eigendecomposition is instant, and 12 leave-one-environment-out folds times 14 traits times three models is a few thousand tiny fits. Embedding hours are zero because the route I propose never touches DNA sequence; the sequence route would need the 12,046,016,411-base reference genome and is excluded on size.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Already run, and it is discouraging. Correlate the paper's own weather-derived index synCov (Table S5) against environment-mean seed yield across the 9 environments that have yield: I get r = -0.218, essentially nothing, and with the wrong sign. Then count the test sets available: 9 environments for seed yield, so leave-one-environment-out gives 9 folds of roughly 205 lines each, and the weather side of the model has 9 data points to learn from. Anyone picking this up should re-run exactly those two lines before doing anything else.

verdict_reason: Every Part A killer passes and I verified each one in the files, which is rare and worth recording: 38,071 plot measurements with zero missing and zero non-numeric values, a units-and-transformation table for all 14 traits, 539,643 markers by 222 samples joining 222 of 222 to the phenotypes, a deposited env_mean column that reproduces to six decimal places, a measurable noise floor from two replicate blocks (21.8% variation for yield, 1.1% for flowering time), real genotype-by-environment re-ranking (median across-environment line-mean correlation +0.474, minimum -0.192), and the single apparent count mismatch explained - the extra 223rd accession is the ungenotyped check variety Tiffany, which also accounts for 535 of the 561 duplicate keys. Model-readiness is 8 of 12 and integration 7 of 8 on a weather join I confirmed is clean. What kills it is the combination of C2 = 0 with an effective sample size of 222 lines and 9-12 environments. The exact task, multi-environment genomic prediction with environmental covariates, is served by several open and honestly evaluated efforts, including a public competition that scores held-out environments directly and a 14-dataset benchmark whose conclusion is that no method dominates; the authors already fitted the standard model and reported 0.75 for mean seed yield. No pretrained backbone helps: the plant DNA language models with open weights would need sequence windows from a 12.0-gigabase reference, and the only backbone that fits is a small-tabular transformer on 222 rows. Three further verified signals point the same way - the reported SNP heritabilities of 0.97 to 0.99 for several field traits are not credible at n = 222 and the authors themselves blame limited sample size; the 299 random coordinates behind the synthetic covariate are in no file, so that method cannot be reproduced; and the synthetic covariate correlates with environment-mean seed yield at only r = -0.218 across the 9 yield environments, so the untested-environment claim rests on the weakest link in the paper. Part J is 5 of 10, below threshold. Keep the dataset: it is genuinely high quality, CC BY 4.0, and the tidy 35,608-row joined table is worth having as one panel in a future multi-panel or multi-crop genotype-by-environment study. Revisit only if several public faba bean panels can be pooled to clear roughly 1,000 lines and 25 or more environments.
